decisions.reason: As a flagship organic line with several variants that has already stayed on the market for two years, it fits the firm's strategic direction and core processing capabilities too well to abandon absent clear failure signals.

The organic poultry snack remains a somewhat narrower option than the core pork and salami range, but after surviving beyond launch it is still worth keeping while demand information continues to accumulate at limited cost.
This premium sharing snack is a close extension of the established salami business, and another year on the market makes it a relatively low-risk option to retain rather than exit.

The organic boiled pork sausage is a very close bio extension of a familiar category, so management would usually keep this young product on offer while early sales and repeat purchase become clearer.

The organic thinly sliced chicken breast line matches the firm's push into organic assortment and convenient formats, making it a reasonable option to continue for another year before judging it definitively.

The organic herb-coated salami is close to the firm's core capabilities but more flavor-niche than the main lines, so it is kept as an option for now though it has a somewhat higher chance of later withdrawal.
